deep.reconstruction:
Context: the cote is Grothendieck's study of pseudo-line arrangements in the real projective plane, using combinatorial maps ('cartes'). This page treats the smallest generic case: three pseudo-lines D_i (i in I, |I| = 3) in general position. They cut RP^2 into the 'hemi-octahedron': 3 vertices, 6 edges and 4 triangular faces. Grothendieck calls this a 'left octahedron' (octaèdre gauche); the next page also calls it 'general' or 'projective'.

The 1-skeleton K is the multigraph on the vertex set I with every pair of vertices joined by two parallel edges.
- Each D_i is a bigon whose vertex set is S_i = I - {i} and whose edge set A_i is a 2-element set (the edges not through vertex i).
- An orientation of D_i is an element of the Z/2-torsor Ω_i = S_i ∧ A_i. Here ∧ is the contracted product of Z/2-torsors, and a 2-element set is viewed as a Z/2-torsor.
- The previous page sets L_i = Ω_i ∧ ∧_{α≠i}(I-{α}) and obtains canonical isomorphisms (15): ∧Ω_i ≅ ∧L_i ≅ (∧A_i) ∧ ∧_α(I-{α}).
- The product ∧_α(I-{α}) is identified with or(I), the orientation (sign) torsor of the 3-element set I.
- Since all of these are defined purely from K and the subgraphs D_i, (15) can be rewritten as (15bis): (∧Ω_i)∧or(I) ≅ (∧L_i)∧or(I) ≅ ∧A_i. The first two terms are read as 'orientation of the octahedron defined by (Ω_i)', respectively by (L_i).

Key point: when K comes from a genuine map C on RP^2, the torsor ∧A_i acquires a canonical trivialisation. Geometrically:
- The graph has 8 'triangles' (pick one edge from each A_i), i.e. the elements of ΠA_i.
- These split into two parity classes modulo even changes; ∧A_i is exactly the torsor of these two classes.
- The 4 face boundaries of the cell structure form one class. They are the contractible triangles; the other 4 are the non-contractible ones, i.e. the class in H_1(RP^2;Z/2).

Statement (16): the functor from left octahedra (2-dimensional cell complexes) to left octahedral graphs equipped with a trivialisation ∧_{i∈I} A_i ≅ 1 is an equivalence of categories. So the 2-cell structure is a Z/2 datum on the 1-skeleton. The margin glosses this extra structure as an 'orientation' of the left octahedral graph.

Diagram (17) is a cube of categories: oriented vs. unoriented, spherical vs. projective ('gauche'), 2-dimensional vs. marked 1-dimensional. For example:
- oct^+ → oct.gauches is an equivalence: the orientation double cover of the hemi-octahedron is the spherical octahedron, and an orientation removes the extra central symmetry, Aut S_4×{±1} vs S_4.
- The vertical arrow from oct.gauches to itself is the identity: projective octahedra are 'automatically oriented'.
- The next page explains which arrows are equivalences, faithful, or surjective on Hom, and the margin there points to S̃_n vs S_n×{±1}.

Purpose: to build a purely combinatorial and torsor-theoretic description of pseudo-line systems, starting with the 3-line case, and to keep track of orientations canonically (without choices) via Z/2-torsors.
errors: The identification ∧_{α∈I}(I-{α}) ≅ or(I) for |I| = 3 checks out: a transposition reverses exactly one pairwise order (the other two pairs are exchanged consistently), so the action is by the sign.
The parity description of the 4 faces among the 8 triangles is correct for three pseudolines in RP^2.
In (17) the bottom arrow oct → oct.gauches is not an equivalence (the next page says it is surjective on Hom); the image agrees.

ideas.what: Hemi-octahedron as the cell structure of three generic pseudo-lines in RP^2; its double cover is the octahedron; orientations and the automorphism groups S_4×{±1} vs S_4
ideas.modern_name: Hemi-octahedron / rank-3 uniform oriented matroid on 3 elements; orientation double cover
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Coxeter for hemi-polyhedra; Folkman–Lawrence 1978 and Grünbaum for pseudoline arrangements)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses regular maps and polyhedra; whether it mentions pseudo-line systems specifically is unsure

ideas.what: Encoding orientations of the pseudo-lines and of the arrangement canonically as Z/2-torsors (contracted products of 2-element sets, with or(I) the sign torsor), giving canonical isomorphisms (15)/(15bis)
ideas.modern_name: Orientation/determinant torsors; sign bookkeeping akin to chirotopes
ideas.usually_credited_to: Chirotope formalism: Dress, Bland–Las Vergnas (1978–80s); torsor/determinant formalism: Knudsen–Mumford, Deligne
ideas.where_published: Torsor language is pervasive in SGA; this specific application is not known to be published

ideas.what: Equivalence (16): left (projective) octahedra ≃ left octahedral graphs with a trivialisation of ∧A_i. The 2-cells are recovered from the 1-skeleton plus a Z/2 parity datum (the contractible triangles)
ideas.modern_name: Recovering a map/cellulation of RP^2 from its graph plus a Z/2 cycle-class (H_1(RP^2;Z/2)) datum, i.e. a signed-graph / embedding-scheme description
ideas.usually_credited_to: Embedding schemes of signed graphs for non-orientable surfaces (Ringel, Stahl, Mohar–Thomassen)

ideas.what: Cube (17) of categories (oriented/unoriented × spherical/projective × 2-dim/marked 1-dim), with the exactness properties of each functor
ideas.modern_name: Categorical comparison of combinatorial models (maps vs graphs, double covers)

missed.claim: A canonical, choice-free torsor formalism for orientations in pseudo-line arrangements. The face structure of the 3-line arrangement is encoded as a trivialisation of the Z/2-torsor ∧A_i, and orientation data are packaged as or(I)-twisted products. This is a functorial 'determinant torsor' viewpoint on chirotope signs that oriented-matroid theory usually handles by fixing sign conventions.
missed.quote: il y a, K provient de la carte C, une trivialisation canon. des Z/2Z-torseurs (15 bis)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is a modest documentary point: it shows Grothendieck developing a functorial, torsor-based approach to oriented-matroid-like structures around 1981, independently of Folkman–Lawrence and Bland–Las Vergnas. Mathematically, the 3-line case itself is elementary.

deep.surprise_reason: Careful, correct, but elementary bookkeeping for the three-pseudoline (hemi-octahedron) case. The torsor-theoretic packaging is characteristic of Grothendieck and historically interesting as evidence of his work on pseudo-line systems, but contains no result a specialist would find new.
transcription_corrections: 'défini... en termes des 1-complexes connus √K' — the inserted word above is probably 'connus' (or 'courbes'), and '√K' is likely the editor's rendering of an insertion caret before K rather than a square root.
'une suppl. d'iso' is more plausibly 'une suite d'iso.'
'or. des l'oct.' under the first term of (15bis) should read 'or. de l'oct.'
In the underlined insertion above 'canon.', the word is most likely 'trivialisation' (the struck word below it is illegible).

In (16), the overbrace 'gr. oct. gauches^+' labels the target 'graphes octaédraux gauches, munis d'une trivialisation ...'; the margin note reads roughly '= gr. oct. avec structure suppl. une orientation des gr. octaédraux gauches'.
In (17) the bottom-row arrow oct → oct.gauches is not marked ≈; there is a short extra stroke near it (likely a surjectivity mark, consistent with the next page).
